clips.name: Probe and zero your stock: simulator and motion previews

steps.caption: Open the fixture plate for setup context. The simulator has its own virtual contact surface.
Control: connect only to the built-in simulator, clear the software stop and Home.
Machine > Diagnostics: read the virtual block position, top Z, bore diameter and surface bow.
Probing > Outside corner: inspect the approach and selected faces before any touch.
Next previews the next motion. A real cycle needs a clear path and a matching fixture.
Bore: establish work Z0 at stock top, start over the bore center, then review the four touches.
Z0 sets the stock-top work reference immediately after a successful touch; no separate Confirm.
Load the fixture-plate setup in Control, then inspect its Z surface grid. Keep every sample on solid stock.
Tool Z records tool length after a successful touch. It is distinct from work Z0 and XY offsets.
This is a simulator and preview tour: no probing cycle or offset write, and no hardware motion.

clips.name: Form a knob: inspect the finished tutorial

steps.caption: Open the shipped Form source: Lobed knob, Shaft profile, Shaft, Bore and Rim fillet.
Right-click Lobed knob > Edit to reopen its cage. Set Circular copies to 4 for the four lobes.
Display > Cage reveals the control points behind the four lobes and finger valleys.
Display > Both shows the cage over the smooth skin. Select points before dragging a move arrow.
The tutorial pulls a lobe out 10 mm, forms 6 mm valleys and lowers the top 8 mm. Here we inspect its saved result.
Display > Smooth inspects the skin without the cage. Finish Form creates an exact solid.
Finish Form rebuilds the saved shaft, 3 mm bore and 1.5 mm rim fillet on the knob.
Display mode > Zebra stripes helps inspect the finished surface continuity.
The Form source creates a model. Open the separate knob machining companion when ready for CAM.

clips.name: Picture to relief: the shipped medallion

steps.caption: Open example 07: a picture relief on a round blank, held inside a 90 x 90 x 8 mm frame.
Edit the saved Relief and open medallion.png. Its target is the medallion face, not another example.
Raise previews the picture above the face. Depth controls its height in millimetres.
Engrave previews the picture cut into the face. Review the height map and the zero plane.
Emboss is the shipped recipe: 2 mm depth across a 24 mm picture on the round blank.
Cancel these preview changes to retain the shipped medallion and its matching CAM recipe.
Regenerate: drill four screw holes, stop to fit screws and remove clamps, rough, finish, then tabbed outline.
Simulate the whole setup to the end. The disc stays tabbed to the complete frame.
On the real job, follow the setup sheet at the operator stop. Cut the tabs after machining, then unscrew the frame.
